what_happened: In job zvmr, the user corrected Athena's first reading of a request about `land_pr`, the landing step. Criterion 3 let a pull request with extra commits on top of the job's landing commit through when the operator declared an intervention. The user replaced it. Until the records-history build (D111) lands, a squash of the landing commit plus any later commit is not a valid landing. Squash 02837e0 broke the history check this way. So `land_pr` must refuse whenever the pull request's current head is anything other than the job's landing commit, declared intervention or not, and it must name the extra commits. Criterion 2's refusal covers all such cases. The rest of the reading stayed: checks and the merge guard are keyed to the current head, and `land_pr` never force-replaces a newer head. The correction came before the work went on.
cause: Athena builds a reading from the request text. It does not pull in the incident that motivated the request, here the squash that broke the history check, or test each criterion against it. Nothing makes the reading state which cases are invalid in themselves and which are only unusual, so it defaulted to a permissive rule that an operator declaration can override. That override is the same hand-bypass route that caused the incident. Only the user's correction exposed it. The reading was right about the topic but wrong on how strict the refusal must be.
prevention: Require a reading of a guard or refusal request to cite the triggering incident. For each criterion it must say whether any override is allowed. Any case that reproduces the incident must be refused with no override path. Add a code check that rejects a reading in which a guard criterion mentions an override or exception without naming a case the incident did not cover. Also add a test for `land_pr` that a pull request whose head is not the landing commit is refused with and without a declared intervention, and that the message names the extra commits.
proposed_request: Make `land_pr` refuse to land any pull request whose current head is not the job's landing commit. This holds whether or not an intervention was declared. Until the records-history build (D111) lands, a squash of a job's landing commit plus any later commit is not a valid landing, and that is how squash 02837e0 broke the history check. The refusal must name the extra commits. Checks and the merge guard must be keyed to the pull request's current head, and `land_pr` must never force-replace a newer head. Show with tests that a head equal to the landing commit lands, that a head with one or more extra commits is refused with the extra commits named, both with and without a declared intervention, and that a newer head is never force-replaced.
